Consider the following data sets:

$$
x={4,\,6,\,8,\,2},\,y={2,\,4,\,10,\,8}
$$

You're given that $\overset{―}{x}=5$ and $\overset{―}{y}=6.$ Calculate $\text{Cov}(x,y).$
after.worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x={{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}}$ and $y={{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(4-5)(2-6)+(6-5)(4-6)+(8-5)(10-6)+(2-5)(8-6)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-1)(-4)+(1)(-2)+(3)(4)+(-3)(2)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[4-2+12-6] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 8 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

First, we need to compute the means:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (4+(-2)+5+1) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 8 \\  & =2 \\ \overset{―}{y} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot ((-7)+5+4+(-2)) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}

after.worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x={{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}}$ and $y={{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(14-16)(62-69)+(16-16)(63-69)+(16-16)(73-69)+(18-16)(78-69)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-2)(-7)+(0)(-6)+(0)(4)+(2)(9)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[14+0+0+18] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 32 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
